title: Instruction Weaving — prompt-rotation & temporal exemplar experiments
body:
Purpose: quick personal scratchpad for 'weaving' exemplars across time windows and prompt rotations. Goal is to find lightweight templates that are robust to order shifts and token budget constraints. Not a final spec — experiments, wobbly thoughts, TODOs, and a few concrete few-shot sets + failure probes.

High-level idea:
- Instead of static few-shot blocks, try staggered exemplar weaving: interleave 1-2 short exemplars at multiple insertion points across the instruction context so the model sees varied positionings of the same signal. Hypothesis: reduces positional overfitting and improves temporal recall when context sliding occurs (e.g., chat truncation).

Quick notes on where this came from:
- Observed brittle re-ranking where the first exemplar dominated decisions when context truncated (prod logs, July–Nov runs).
- Slack thread #prompt-lab: Samir called this "slot-rotation" (he liked slot language). I prefer 'weaving' because samples can overlap across slots.

Minimal templates to test (keep <= 4 exemplars total under 1k tokens):
1) Anchor + weave template (short):
   INSTRUCTION:
   \u003cTASK\u003e

   SLOT A (exemplar):
   - Q: How to summarize the gist of a paragraph?
   - A: Pick the main claim and supporting evidence in 1-2 sentences.

   SLOT B (weave):
   - Q: How to shorten code comments?
   - A: Remove repetition, keep intent, one-line.

   USER INPUT:
   \u003cUSER_TEXT\u003e

2) Rotating exemplar set (explicit positions):
   [INSTR]
   [EX1: style exemplar]
   [CTX]
   [EX2: summary exemplar]
   [USER_PROMPT]

3) Temporal annealing: keep exemplar order variable across calls (random seed) so model cannot rely on example order only. Track per-seed metrics.

Concrete few-shot examples (very short):
- EX1 (style):
  Q: Rewrite to professional tone:
  Input: "hey team, this is a heads up"
  Output: "Hi team, please note the following update."

- EX2 (summ):
  Q: Summarize in two sentences:
  Input: "Service X failed after deploy due to missing config. Restart fixed it."
  Output: "After the deploy, Service X failed because a configuration was omitted. A restart restored normal operation."

- EX3 (fix-it):
  Q: Identify action and owner:
  Input: "DB migration skipped index creation"
  Output: "Action: recreate index; Owner: backend-oncall"

Failure probes to include in the eval set:
- Order flip: same exemplars but opposite order. Measure label/score drift.
- Truncation simulation: cut the leftmost 150 tokens (simulate sliding window) and score output fidelity.
- Cross-task contamination: include exemplars with similar labels but different granularity (summary vs highlight) to see cross-talk.

Observations so far (notes from quick runs):
- 2025-12-03 run: weaving with 3 slots reduced order-sensitivity on summarization (approx 12% fewer anchor-dominant mistakes), but introduced more hallucinated owner tags in fix-it tasks (likely because we duplicated owner-bearing exemplars across slots).
- 2025-12-11: Rotating-seed helped overall robustness but increased variance; need N=100 seeds to smooth.

Short ablation plan:
- A: Static block (baseline) vs B: Two-slot weave vs C: Three-slot staggered weave.
- Metric: task accuracy, hallucination rate (owner & date hallucinations), token efficiency (avg tokens used in reply).
- Sample size: 500 prompts per condition, stratified by length bins (short/medium/long).

Toy evaluation harness notes (how I ran locally):
- Runner: local harness that hits hosted API with prompt envelope. Script randomizes exemplar order or slot population. Writes CSV of seed, attempt_id, condition, tokens_in, tokens_out, task_label, model_pred, confidence.
- Quick command: python run_weave_experiment.py --cond staggered --seed 42 --n 200 --model redwood-v-small

Known risks / edge cases:
- Doubling exemplar content across slots increases token footprint; need to balance duplication vs diversity.
- For function-calling structured outputs, weaving can confuse schema if exemplar labels differ (e.g., "owner" vs "assignee"). Standardize labels in exemplars.

Brainstormed variants to try next:
- Soft anchors: use a one-line anchor describing desired output format that repeats in each slot, but vary exemplar content. Anchors should be format-only (no label tokens).
- Token-aware weaving: prefer short exemplars in early slots and longer ones later for cost-smoothing.
- Conditional weaving: pick exemplars based on detected user intent cluster (cheap classifier) rather than random.

Example debug case (raw):
- Prompt: "Summarize incident and who fixed it."
- Baseline output (static first-exemplar bias): "Restart fixed Service X. Owner: infra" (wrong owner)
- Weave output (better): "Service X failed after deploy due to missing config; restart restored service. Owner: backend-oncall." (correct when we included fix-it exemplar in a later slot)

TODOs (short):
- [ ] Convert promising variant into a reusable prompt template in prompt library (GH PR stub created).
- [ ] Add structured exemplar canonicalization step to avoid label synonyms.
- [ ] Run 1k-sample stability sweep across seeds and log distribution.
- [ ] Add as an option in cheap classifier routing experiment (link to JIRA-ML-987).

Open questions (notes to self):
- Does weaving meaningfully help for long-form generation tasks ( > 800 tokens ) or only short structured outputs?
- At what duplication threshold does token overhead negate robustness gains?
- Can we derive a small predictor that decides number of slots dynamically per prompt?

Random scratch ideas (one-liners):
- "exemplar seasoning": lightly paraphrase same exemplar into multiple surface forms before weaving.
- "slot sweeps": slowly shift exemplar content rightward for subsequent requests in a session (helpful for chat continuity).

If you read this later: quick checks to run first: order-flip test, truncation-left test at 150 tokens, short/long length split. Save results CSV in /tmp/weave_runs and upload best configs to prompt-library PR.

End of scratchpad. Expect lots of churn. Keep it short and iterative.
